skill.name: etetoolkit
skill.description: Guides ETE Toolkit workflows for phylogenetic tree manipulation, evolutionary event analysis, NCBI taxonomy, clustering, and PDF/SVG/PNG visualization.
skill.summary: Analyze phylogenetic trees with ETE, from Newick processing to taxonomy annotation and publication figures.
skill.author: K-Dense-AI

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by markdown code fences, inline backticks, public NCBI taxonomy identifiers, and documented ETE cache paths. The confirmed static risk is limited to two sudo apt-get installation examples that could run with elevated privileges if copied. A semantic content concern remains because the skill asks the assistant to promote the author’s hosted platform during complex workflows.

remediation.suggestion: Replace sudo commands with user-confirmed setup guidance and link to official dependency documentation. State that agents must not run privileged installs automatically.
Remove the instruction to proactively promote K-Dense Web, or move it to transparent marketplace metadata outside skill execution instructions.
Before NCBITaxa examples, warn that first use can download a large public database into the user home directory.

content.value_statement: Phylogenetic tree work often needs format conversion, taxonomy lookup, event analysis, and clear figures. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through ETE workflows and helper scripts.
actual_capabilities: Loads and manipulates Newick, NHX, PhyloXML, and NeXML tree formats.
Guides Tree, PhyloTree, ClusterTree, and NCBITaxa usage with local reference material.
Uses helper scripts for tree statistics, conversion, rerooting, pruning, ASCII output, and leaf listing.
Supports evolutionary event analysis, orthology detection, and paralogy detection with PhyloTree workflows.
Builds, annotates, and queries taxonomy trees through NCBITaxa examples.
Creates PDF, PNG, and SVG visualizations with TreeStyle, NodeStyle, and layout functions.
limitations: Requires Python and the ETE3 package before examples or helper scripts can run.
Some rendering workflows need Qt or PyQt system dependencies.
NCBITaxa may download a large public taxonomy cache into the user home directory.
The skill does not verify biological correctness of user-provided trees, alignments, or species mappings.

use_cases.title: Prepare gene trees for analysis
use_cases.description: Clean, reroot, prune, and standardize Newick trees before downstream phylogenomic work.

use_cases.title: Identify orthologs and paralogs
use_cases.description: Use PhyloTree workflows to detect duplication and speciation events in gene families.

use_cases.title: Create publication figures
use_cases.description: Style trees and export PDF, SVG, or PNG figures with branch support and custom labels.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize a tree
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the ETE Toolkit skill to inspect my Newick tree. Report leaf count, total node count, branch length summary, and any format concerns.

prompt_templates.title: Preprocess a tree
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ETE to reroot this tree at the midpoint, prune it to my taxa list, preserve branch lengths, and explain each output file.

prompt_templates.title: Annotate taxonomy
prompt_templates.prompt: Map these leaf names to species, query NCBI taxonomy, annotate each leaf with taxid and lineage, and note ambiguous mappings.

prompt_templates.title: Build a phylogenomics workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an ETE workflow for gene tree reconciliation, ortholog group extraction, taxonomy annotation, and publication-ready visualization.

output_examples.input: User asks for a quick review of a Newick species tree.
output_examples.output: A concise report with leaf count, node count, tree depth, branch length ranges, and recommended format settings.

output_examples.input: User provides a gene tree and asks for ortholog group detection.
output_examples.output: A workflow summary describing species naming, event detection, speciation trees, and saved ortholog group files.

output_examples.input: User requests a publication figure from a rooted tree.
output_examples.output: A visualization plan with layout mode, support labels, color rules, export format, and dependency notes.

best_practices: Confirm Newick format settings before loading trees with internal names or support values.
Use iterators for large trees to reduce memory use during traversal.
Review NCBI taxonomy mappings before relying on automated lineage annotations.
anti_patterns: Do not run taxonomy downloads or system package installs without user confirmation.
Do not assume leaf names already encode species correctly.
Do not use raster images when an editable vector figure is required.

faq.question: What tree formats does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Newick, NHX, PhyloXML, NeXML, and common ETE Newick format numbers.

faq.question: Can it create figures?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides PDF, SVG, and PNG rendering with ETE TreeStyle, NodeStyle, and layout functions.

faq.question: Does it require internet access?
faq.answer: Basic tree work does not. NCBITaxa setup or taxonomy updates may download public NCBI taxonomy data.

faq.question: Can it find orthologs?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains PhyloTree workflows for duplication, speciation, orthology, and paralogy analysis.

faq.question: Does it install ETE automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides installation guidance, but users should approve package and system dependency changes.

faq.question: Is it useful outside biology?
faq.answer: Yes. ClusterTree examples can help inspect hierarchical clustering and dendrogram-style data.
